headline: Anthropic shares sink on day two, dragging the Nasdaq
dek: The Guardian and CNBC report the Claude maker fell near its IPO price in a broad selloff.

s2.label: What happened
s2.title: Down near the IPO price
body: Shares fell 9% on Friday (Nov 20) and closed at $88.30, near the $83 IPO price (The Guardian).
On day one the stock closed up 17% (The Guardian, CNBC).

s3.label: How it works
s3.title: The selloff spread
s3.body: The drop came alongside a broad pullback in markets.

points.t: Erased 2026 gains and closed 5% below its January 1 level (The Guardian).
Fell 14% on Friday, according to The Guardian.
Lost 14.5% in Tokyo, its worst day in over two years (The Guardian).

s4.label: Why it matters
s4.title: Doubts over AI returns
body: Analyst Daniela Hathorn says AI demand is strong, but doubts over valuations and spending remain (The Guardian).
Amodei says the $900 billion in commitments look smaller than they are (CNBC).

items.t: Chris Beauchamp says Anthropic may drain market liquidity (The Guardian).
The Dow and S&P 500 entered correction territory (The Guardian).
Bitcoin and gold also fell this week (The Guardian, CNBC).

caption.hook: Anthropic shares sink on day two and drag the Nasdaq lower.
body: Anthropic shares fell 9% on Friday and closed at $88.30, near the $83 IPO price, according to the Guardian. On day one the stock had closed up 17% (The Guardian, CNBC). The drop came in a broad selloff: Nvidia lost 14% and SoftBank fell 14.5% in Tokyo (The Guardian).

The Nasdaq erased its 2026 gains, and the Dow and S&P 500 entered correction territory (The Guardian). Analyst Daniela Hathorn says AI demand is strong, but doubts over valuations and spending persist. Dario Amodei defended $900 billion in commitments (CNBC).
caption.cta: Is this a healthy correction for AI stocks or the start of a bigger slide?
